correctness.rationale: If an outer pair is initially empty, its twin vertices cannot be entered by a first force. With the center blue, meeting every pair lets each singly represented pair complete. With the center white, exactly one selected vertex in every pair gives no first force, while any full pair forces the center and then all singly represented pairs. The two disjoint cases count to the displayed polynomial. The inspected verifier exhaustively checks all subsets for \(1\le k\le8\); independent brute force reproduced the full coefficient vectors through \(k=5\).

value.rationale: Friendship graphs are a standard infinite family, and the theorem determines the entire zero-forcing-set distribution rather than only the minimum number. The simple pair-occupancy mechanism supplies an exact reusable benchmark for graph-operation and counting questions.

final_claim: For the friendship graph \(F_k\), \(k\ge1\), a zero-forcing set containing the center meets every outer pair, while a center-free zero-forcing set meets every outer pair and fully contains at least one pair. Consequently \(\mathcal Z(F_k;x)=x^k((1+x)(2+x)^k-2^k)\), \(Z(F_k)=k+1\), with \(2^{k-1}(k+2)\) minimum sets.
limitations: Ordinary zero forcing on friendship graphs only.
No claim is made for other windmill block sizes or forcing variants.
